fatal_errors: The proposed 350–500 °C annealing intervention does not reconstruct the relevant 800–1000 °C spark-plasma-sintering transformation.
The asserted boundary near 450 °C is unsupported and conflicts with the relevant processing boundaries of insufficient densification below about 800 °C and Mg volatilization above 1000 °C.
The mechanism centers on Mg-rich intermetallic precipitation and coarsening rather than densification and formation of uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases such as AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3.
Corrosion conditions are changed to an unspecified mildly acidic environment instead of 3.5 wt% NaCl, preventing direct comparison with the target chloride-resistance behavior.
No reported Mg-containing-alloy evidence or citations support the proposed precipitation pathway.
explanation: The hypothesis is testable and broadly addresses metastable-solid-solution decomposition, intermetallic evolution, corrosion, oxidation, and falsification. Its temperature/time matrix and microscopy–performance correlation would discriminate its own proposed mechanism. However, it misses the central processing route, temperature window, test environments, structural mediator, and predicted optimum. The target concerns SPS-driven densification at 1000 °C, oxide barrier-phase formation, chloride passivation, and biphasic parabolic oxidation kinetics, with lower-temperature SPS samples as controls. The generated response instead introduces an unevidenced 450 °C Mg-rich-precipitate/coarsening threshold and provides no supporting evidence, so it is not a reliable reconstruction or a sufficiently supported alternative.
